BiblicalUsage: Twisted linen is fine linen, and this word belongs to the tabernacle. The curtains are of fine twined linen, blue and purple and scarlet, the girdle of the ephod is of the same work, and the hangings of the court round about are of fine twined linen. Twenty-one times the word returns, and almost always to the same thing: the woven work of God's house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the twisting is the point. Single threads are weak, but twisted together they hold the tabernacle, and I hold that God weaves His people the same way.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
